text:
elena: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in dropped spans from the GPU pool after the collector gateway started fanout routing to regional collectors. Prometheus alert fired: otel_collector_spans_dropped_total > 100 in 5m. logs:
```
ERROR otel.collector span_processor.go:142 span dropped: missing parent_id, dropped by fanout worker
```
Any ideas whether this is gateway propagation or SDK sampling?

ops-bot: Alert: otel_collector_spans_dropped_total (gpu-pool-prod) triggered at 1790012330 :fire:. Pager duty: infra-oncall.

tariq: I saw this too. Quick checks: 1) gateway uses gRPC fanout to multi-region collectors; 2) our envoy config might be stripping trace headers during mTLS pass-through. Can someone confirm if traceparent is in the upstream headers on fanout requests?

simon: I pulled an example request from L7 logs — traceparent present when hitting gateway, but absent at regional collector ingress. Looks like the HTTP->gRPC translation step in the collector gateway isn't copying the W3C trace headers into gRPC metadata.

maria: That explains it. SDK side sampling is default always_on, so this is not sampling. It's header propagation. We should either ensure the gateway maps headers or make the collector accept both traceparent and grpc-* metadata keys.

ajay: Quick mitigation: bump sampling to probabilistic 0.1 on the runtime for GPU-heavy routes so less spans are sent while we patch header mapping. Also propose a rule in gateway to sticky-route by session id so we avoid cross-region fanout for the same request flow (reduces chance of reparenting).

elena: Agree on mitigation. Two action items: (1) Add header mapping in gateway config — copy traceparent -> grpc-trace-bin and trace-state into metadata. Example patch snippet:
```
# gateway filter
filters:
  - name: header_to_metadata
    config:
      request_rules:
        - header: traceparent
          on_header_present:
            metadata_namespace: otel
            key: traceparent
```
(2) Short-term: lower sampling at runtime as ajay suggested + silence the Prom alert to avoid noise (we'll re-enable after fix).

tariq: I'll open a PR for the gateway header mapping and add an e2e test that asserts traceparent survives fanout. Also will add a Grafana panel showing "spans dropped by reason" so we can quickly see if it's header-loss vs overload.

maria: For the alert tuning, let's not mute completely — change the alert to fire on sustained high drop rate (5m -> 15m window) and only for > 500 drops, plus add a playbook link. Otherwise we get paged for churny transient issues.

simon: FYI we also saw a small correlation with GPU autoscaler events — when nodes are replaced we saw more header loss. Could be transient LB stickiness or healthcheck path that strips headers. I'll instrument the autoscaler path to preserve headers across kube-proxy healthcheck redirects.

elena: Great. Owners: tariq -> gateway PR + test; simon -> autoscaler header preservation; ajay -> sampling change and sticky-route experiment; maria -> alert update + playbook. I'll follow up in an ops runbook issue. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: Created issue INFRA-9327 "gateway: preserve trace headers during fanout" and linked playbook. Assigned: tariq.

ajay: Rolling sampling change now to canary (gpu-pool-canary). Will monitor spans/sec and metrics: otel_exporter_sent_spans_total and otel_collector_spans_dropped_total.

elena: Thanks team — keep updates here. If anyone notices end-to-end traces dropping after the gateway patch, ping infra-oncall immediately.
